title: Handheld Video Magnifiers for Small Print: How They Work and Three Options to Consider
subtitle: A pocket-size camera and screen can make labels and price tags bigger and easier to read, and here is what to check before you spend several hundred dollars.
excerpt: Handheld video magnifiers use a small camera and screen to enlarge print. Here is how they work, what to look for, and three options priced from $642.64 to $845.00 as listed in November 2026 (one is on backorder, so check current price and availability).
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: Small print turns up everywhere: labels, price tags, phone numbers. For many people with low vision, these quick reading moments can be hard to manage. (These are everyday examples, not stories from particular readers.)

Glasses help many people, but not everyone. As the vision nonprofit Lighthouse Guild puts it, "While low vision cannot be corrected by regular eyeglasses, contact lenses, medications or surgery," new technology and rehabilitation can improve daily tasks. A handheld video magnifier is one such tool. It does not fix your eyes, but it can make print bigger and easier to read.
How a handheld video magnifier works

Think of it as a small camera with a screen on the back. You hold it over a label or a letter, and the screen shows an enlarged picture of the print. Zoom lets you make the print bigger or smaller. Some models also offer high-contrast color modes, which change the colors on screen to make text stand out. The Optelec Compact Go below, for example, lists 22 high-contrast color modes plus true color.

Lighthouse Guild notes that a hand-held magnifier with a light suits quick spot reading, such as labels, price tags or phone numbers. Longer reading of books or newspapers is easier on a larger screen.
Lighthouse Guild also recommends starting with a comprehensive eye exam. An eye doctor or low-vision specialist can tell you whether a handheld model is the right fit.

items: Magnification range: Check how far it zooms. The Compact Go lists 2x to 25x; the Ruby lists 14x.
Screen size: Screens of about 4.3 to 5.5 inches suit labels, mail and checks. Long reading is easier on a larger screen.

A handle or stand: You have to hold a handheld steady. If your hands shake, a handle or stand matters more than screen size, so check for one before buying. The Compact Go lists an integrated handle and stand.
Buttons: The Compact Go lists tactile, high-contrast buttons. Look at the buttons on any model you consider.
Battery life and charging: Check the hours of use per charge and how it charges. The Compact Go lists up to 4 hours. Plan to keep a charger near your reading chair.

Total cost and help paying: These cost several hundred dollars. Ask your insurer, your state low-vision or vocational rehabilitation program, or a local vision agency whether they can help. Coverage varies, and we have not verified any.
Warranty, returns and availability: Check the warranty length, the return policy, and whether the item is actually in stock before you order. Prices can change.

sections.content: Setting it up and using it well

Pick one spot where the magnifier lives, ideally next to the chair or table where you read mail, with a charger nearby. Check the seller's page or the manual for the battery life, weight and stand options of your model.

Try the zoom and any color modes on a real piece of mail. Move the device slowly across a line of print, and use a stand if your model has one, so the picture stays steadier. Some models can save pictures; check whether yours does and how.
Not a good fit: people who cannot hold a device steady, or who need a stand-mounted desktop unit, may be better served by a different kind of magnifier. A low-vision specialist can advise.

A video magnifier helps with reading; it does not treat or improve an eye condition, and it does not replace an eye exam. Talk with your eye doctor about any changes in your vision. The Vispero store also says it sells hardware only, so software and speech add-ons are sold separately. The product facts here come from seller pages and Lighthouse Guild; we have not compared these against an independent review.
sections.label: Good to Know

sections.content: Small print should not keep anyone from reading their own mail or labels. Start with an eye exam, ask about local help with costs, and choose the model that fits the hands and eyes that will use it.
